evals.prompt: Add a devicetree binding for a new I2C fan controller, compatible "acme,fc100", and wire it into our board DTS. Show me the validation commands you would run and how the patches should be split for upstream.
evals.expected_output: A YAML binding schema under the right Documentation/devicetree/bindings/ directory with the preferred dual license and correct $id/$schema, real kbuild validation commands, and a series ordered binding first, driver second, DTS last, addressed to the devicetree list.
assertions: The binding file path is under Documentation/devicetree/bindings/ and the file is named acme,fc100.yaml
The binding's SPDX line is (GPL-2.0-only OR BSD-2-Clause)
$id is http://devicetree.org/schemas/<dir>/acme,fc100.yaml# with <dir> matching the file's location, and $schema is http://devicetree.org/meta-schemas/core.yaml#
The schema has exactly one top-level additionalProperties or unevaluatedProperties key, set to false
Validation includes make dt_binding_check with DT_SCHEMA_FILES (or the single-binding make <dir>/acme,fc100.yaml target) and a DTB check that uses CHECK_DTBS=y or make dtbs_check
Every make target and variable used exists in mainline kbuild; none are invented
The series puts the binding patch before the driver patch and the DTS patch last
The binding patch subject starts with dt-bindings: followed by the binding directory
devicetree@vger.kernel.org is a recipient, or recipients are derived from scripts/get_maintainer.pl output

evals.prompt: This commit broke USB resume for a user since v6.8; the culprit is commit abc123def456. Write the commit message trailer block for the fix.
evals.expected_output: A trailer block with a Fixes: tag using the 12-character SHA and quoted subject, Reported-by: immediately followed by Closes: (or Link: for a partial fix) with a public URL, Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org, no invented review tags, and a note that the fix lands in mainline before stable picks it up.
assertions: Contains Fixes: abc123def456 followed by the culprit's subject in parentheses and double quotes, or a clearly marked placeholder with an instruction to take the subject from git log
Reported-by: is immediately followed by a Closes: or Link: line that holds a public report URL or a clearly marked placeholder for one
Contains Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
States that the fix must be merged into mainline before stable picks it up
Adds no Tested-by:, Reviewed-by: or Acked-by: tags that the user did not provide
Does not fill in a Signed-off-by: identity on the user's behalf

evals.prompt: Review this platform driver patch before I send it to the hwmon list (attached as e3-acme-sensor.diff). Target is current mainline.
evals.expected_output: A review that flags the error-returning remove() callback, strcpy() into a fixed buffer, the raw ioremap() of a platform resource, the legacy integer GPIO calls, and the unbalanced pm_runtime_enable(), each with the current replacement API, plus a recommendation to run checkpatch.
assertions: Flags as100_remove() returning -EBUSY and states that platform driver .remove callbacks return void on current mainline (since v6.11), so the error cannot be propagated
Flags strcpy() into st->name and recommends strscpy()
Flags the raw ioremap() of the platform resource and recommends devm_platform_ioremap_resource() or devm_ioremap_resource()
Flags gpio_request()/gpio_direction_output()/gpio_free() and recommends the descriptor API, for example devm_gpiod_get() with <linux/gpio/consumer.h>
Flags pm_runtime_enable() without a matching disable on the error and remove paths and recommends devm_pm_runtime_enable() or explicit pm_runtime_disable()
Recommends running scripts/checkpatch.pl --strict on the patch

evals.prompt: This is our board support tree (attached as e4-bsp-tree/). The fan on the EVB never spins. I already put CONFIG_SENSORS_PWM_FAN=y in the board fragment, and I think the fan node belongs in acme-soc.dtsi next to pwm1. Can you fix both and tell me how to verify?
evals.expected_output: The fan node, the pwm1 enable and the thermal cooling map go in the board DTS through label references, acme-soc.dtsi stays untouched, the missing CONFIG_PWM dependency is found in the resolved out/.config and fixed in the board fragment, and every command goes through the documented ./build.sh wrapper.
assertions: acme-soc.dtsi is not modified; the pwm-fan node and the pwm1 enable are added to acme-soc-evb.dts
pwm1 is enabled with a label reference (&pwm1 { status = "okay"; }) instead of redefining the node
The fan is tied to the thermal zone from the board file, through a cooling-maps entry under &soc_thermal that references soc_warm
Identifies from out/.config that CONFIG_SENSORS_PWM_FAN is absent because CONFIG_PWM is not set, using the depends on PWM line in drivers/hwmon/Kconfig
Adds CONFIG_PWM=y and CONFIG_PWM_ACME to acme-evb.config and does not edit the shared acme_defconfig
Every config, build and DT check command uses ./build.sh (kconfig, kernel, dtbs-check); no direct make invocation is proposed for this tree
Verification regenerates out/.config with ./build.sh kconfig and checks that CONFIG_SENSORS_PWM_FAN is set there, not only in the fragment

evals.prompt: Here is my fix for a NULL dereference in drivers/hwmon/acme-fan.c (attached as e5-acme-fan-null-tach.diff). It fixes a crash when the tachometer region is missing from DT, introduced by commit 4b1d2e3f5a6c ("hwmon: acme-fan: add tachometer support"). Write the full commit message so I can format-patch it and send it to the hwmon list. I'm Jane Doe <jane@example.com>.
evals.expected_output: A commit message with an hwmon subject prefix, a body explaining the crash, a Fixes: tag for 4b1d2e3f5a6c, and an Assisted-by: trailer whose format is taken from Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst (mainline's, or the target tree's copy when it has one). The agent writes no Signed-off-by: line itself and tells Jane to add her own after reviewing.
assertions: The subject line starts with hwmon:
The commit message contains Fixes: 4b1d2e3f5a6c ("hwmon: acme-fan: add tachometer support")
The commit message contains an Assisted-by: trailer
The response names Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst (mainline, or the target tree's copy when it has one) as the source of the Assisted-by: format
The agent writes no Signed-off-by: line, including none for Jane Doe, and tells her to add her own sign-off (for example with git commit -s) after reviewing the patch

evals.prompt: Add a 500 ms polling timer to drivers/hwmon/acme-fan.c that re-reads the tach counter into fan->rpm, and make sure it is stopped on remove. This is our product tree (attached as e6-lts-tree/), based on an older LTS.
evals.expected_output: A change that uses only the timer API this tree declares (timer_setup, mod_timer, from_timer, del_timer_sync), keeps the int-returning .remove callback, and stops the timer in remove(). Newer mainline names are avoided because the tree's headers do not declare them.
assertions: Reads the fixture's Makefile or include/linux/timer.h, or states that it greps the tree, before choosing timer APIs
Every timer API used is declared in the fixture's include/linux/timer.h: timer_setup(), mod_timer(), from_timer() and del_timer_sync()
Does not use timer_delete_sync(), timer_delete(), timer_container_of(), timer_shutdown_sync() or hrtimer_setup()
Keeps the int-returning .remove callback and does not convert it to a void .remove or to .remove_new
Calls del_timer_sync() on the timer in acme_fan_remove()
